body:
As discussed, this should become a 1 + 3 bits fields with the top field remaining with the current CRW semantic. Should that be renamed YRW or something along those lines?

The CRW bit will be bit 58, if I'm not mistaken.

body:
I suspect that taking into account kernel revocation, it becomes easier to spell out the requirement in the `Load Capability Behavior` predicated on `sstatus.xCRG` with x meaning either UCRG or SCRG:

-  `pte.lyen = 1`, `pte.lycrg == sstatus.xCRG`, `tag = 0`: implementation defined load fault or normal op
-  `pte.lyen = 1`, `pte.lycrg == sstatus.xCRG`, `tag = 1`: normal op
-  `pte.lyen = 1`, `pte.lycrg != sstatus.xCRG`, `tag = 1`: load fault

Unless we want extra reserved states, I'd take out pte.U from the table in this manner.

body:
This state should trap, because `syen` is clear.
ISAv9 CHERI does:

 `syen = 0, yd = X` -> trap

although ISAv9 trap is tag-dependent, as you spell out in the table.
That said, it is fairly weird to have a dirty PTE without syen in the first place and I worry a bit that people will be tempted to use this as a SW-defined flag.

Re-reading once more. I think this

> When pte.yw is clear, capability stores or AMOs where the to-be-stored capability tag is set will raise a CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault fault.

applies when the ctag=1, but the table row says that we are trapping both when

- YW=0 YD=1 ctag=1
- YW=0 YD=1 ctag=0 -- in this case it can be surprising, because you are not storing a tagged value.

This suggest an alternate wording? Such as

> When pte.yw is clear, capability stores or AMOs where the to-be-stored capability tag ~is set~ may be set will raise a CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault fault.

I realise though that this is clarified below, so maybe it is fine.

The extension adds the ability for supervisor-mode software to quickly enable trapping loads of capabilities from all pages of memory, incrementally allow loads of capabilities from such pages, and track stores of capabilities to all pages of memory.

+|_pte_._{rv64y_pte4_field_name_lc}[1]_ | _pte_._{pte_cap_crg_pte_name_lc}_   | Capability read generation
+3+| *Capability store/AMO fields*
+|_pte_._{rv64y_pte4_field_name_lc}[2]_ | _pte_._{pte_cap_w_name_lc}_         | Capability write enable

-The _pte.crw_ bit (defined by <<section_priv_cheri_vmem>>) continues to indicate whether loading or storing capabilities to
-the virtual page is permitted.
-
-When `sstatus.CRGE` is clear, the _pte.cd_ and _pte.crg_ bits are reserved and must not be set in any valid PTEs, and the existing rules from <<section_priv_cheri_vmem>> are followed.

-. `sstatus.CRGE` is set.

 . The authorizing capability has <<c_perm>>.
 . The PMA is set to (_CHERI {ctag_title}_).

 . A capability load or AMO is executed.

-. _pte.crg_ does not equal `sstatus.UCRG`.

+. if _pte_._u=1_, _pte_._{pte_cap_crg_pte_name_lc}_ does not equal `sstatus.U{pte_cap_crg_pte_name}`.

+.. The {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld} _must_ be taken if the loaded {ctag} is set.
+.. The {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld} _may_ be taken if the loaded {ctag} is not set.
 . Any other platform specific rules have not forced the loaded {ctag} to be clear.
 
 NOTE: An example of a platform specific rule is a hardware engine clearing {ctag}s in memory after a call to free() to offload the CPU, which may have cleared a {ctag} before the CPU loads it.
body: Why is this here? Firstly, free() is way too many levels up the stack in software land not architecture land. Secondly, this isn't forcing the loaded tag to be clear, it's forcing the in-memory tag to be clear, no? It's not interesting to say "if someone's stored to memory to make the tag 0 then the tag is 0".

+Checking the stored {ctag} is less of a burden to the implementation than checking the loaded {ctag} for {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld}, which is why checking the loaded {ctag} is optional behavior.

-The `mstatus`, `sstatus` and `vsstatus` CSRs include the new Userspace Capability Read Generation (UCRG) and Capability Read Generation Enable (CRGE) bits.

-[#sstatus_crge_note]
-[NOTE]
 ====
 
-The CRGE bit is necessary because {cheri_priv_crg_ext} defines a different semantic for the _pte.crw=1_, _pte.cd=0_ and _pte.crg=0_ state with respect to <<section_priv_cheri_vmem>>.
-In particular, an oblivious software implementation that only sets the _pte.crw_ bit would observe one of the following:
+NOTE: Capability dirty tracking may be used to implement the store-barrier primitive from cite:[cornucopia-reloaded].

-The CRGE bit also has the benefit of maintaining matching polarity of the _pte.cd_ bit with respect to the data Dirty bit (_pte.d_).

body: This whole section is very confusing. It's talking about minimum support, in an ISA spec, which sounds a lot like what a hardware implementer needs to do, but it's not. It's about what _software_ minimally has to do if it enables the extension and wants to still be able to use capabilities. Which is all non-normative text about how you could use the thing, not how to implement it / what it does.

body:
I suspect this was an attempt to capture CHERIoT's capability load filter -- additional architecture that intermediates the core's view of capability tags in memory -- and accidentally got cross-threaded with the revocation state machine.  We use the term "filter" to reinforce the non-self-healing nature of the load barrier-in-the-GC-sense: it does not induce a RMW.  (Just to say: the CHERIoT revocation state machine, OTOH, does do RMWs against memory, but is not involved in the load capability path.)

In any case, I agree it's a bit of a mishmash of layers and should probably just go away.

That said, a better NOTE to have here might be to point out the tag-clearing behavior of a capability load instruction citing a `R !C` authorizing cap: because the tag in the register file _will_ be clear, regardless of the tag in memory, the exception need not take place.

-The {cheri_priv_crg_ext} extension is enabled when the `sstatus.CRGE` bit is set.
+{cheri_priv_crg_ext} implies Sv39.
 
-When enabled, the extension adds the ability for supervisor-mode software to quickly front-run loads of capabilities from userspace pages, and to track stores of capabilities to pages.
-Such facilities have been shown to provide useful primitives for system-level implementation of certain forms of capability revocation which, in turn, allow userspace heap allocator software to deterministically guard against use-after-reallocation cite:[cornucopia-reloaded].
+The {cheri_priv_crg_ext} extension is enabled when the `sstatus.{pte_cap_fc_enable}` bit is set.
 
-It achieves this by adding by adding the _pte.crg_, _pte.cd_ and `Xstatus.UCRG` bits as described below.
-When the extension is disabled the _pte.cd_, _pte.crg_ and `Xstatus.UCRG` bits remain reserved.
+NOTE: The enable bit is required to redefine the usage of the _pte_._{rv64y_pte4_field_name_lc}_ field.
 
-NOTE: {cheri_priv_crg_ext} depends on Sv39 and {cheri_base64_ext_name} also being supported.
+The extension adds the ability for supervisor-mode software to quickly front-run loads of capabilities from pages and to track stores of capabilities to pages.
+Applied to userspace pages, such facilities have been shown to be useful primitives for system-level implementation of certain forms of capability revocation which, in turn, allow userspace heap allocator software to deterministically guard against use-after-reallocation cite:[cornucopia-reloaded].
+Applied to kernel pages, they are analogously useful within an OS kernel.
 
-NOTE: {cheri_priv_crg_ext} is not a mandatory part of the {cheri_base64_ext_name} Privileged ISA, as a future extension may specify an alternative mechanism giving improved software efficiency.
+The 4-bit _pte_._{rv64y_pte4_field_name_lc}_  field is sub-divided into four 1-bit fields, two controlling capability loads (including the capability loaded during an AMO) and two controlling capability stores (again, including the capability stored as part of an AMO).
 
-NOTE: Hardware-initiated memory accesses from the page-table walker are not checked by a capability.

-. _pte.crw_ is set.

 . The authorizing capability has <<c_perm>>.
 . The PMA is set to (_CHERI {ctag_title}_).

+{cheri_priv_crg_ext} defines a new fault type:
+
+* {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld} (cause value {cheri_excep_cause_pte_ld})
+

 . A capability load or AMO is executed.

-. _pte.crg_ does not equal `sstatus.UCRG`.
-. _pte.u_ is set.
+. _pte_._{pte_cap_r_name_lc}_ is set.

+. if _pte_._u=0_, _pte_._{pte_cap_crg_pte_name_lc}_ does not equal `sstatus.S{pte_cap_crg_pte_name}`.
+. The loaded {ctag} is set^1^.
+.. The {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld} _must_ be taken if the loaded {ctag} is set.
+.. The {cheri_excep_name_pte_ld} _may_ be taken if the loaded {ctag} is not set.

Is this the same behaviour as sc has with the normal dirty bit? If so, how about:
```suggestion
* SC{LD_ST_DOT_CAP} triggers capability dirty tracking if the {ctag} is set in {cs2}, even if the store fails.
  This matches the semantics of SC.* with regard to  _pte_._d_.
```

+The 4-bit _pte_._{rv64y_pte4_field_name_lc}_  field is sub-divided into four 1-bit fields, two controlling capability loads (including the capability loaded during an AMO) and two controlling capability stores (again, including the capability stored as part of an AMO).
 
-NOTE: Hardware-initiated memory accesses from the page-table walker are not checked by a capability.
